hook: After hostel fire, students say *10 per room* at GMC Narayanpet
hook_b: After hostel fire, students say *10 per room* at GMC Narayanpet
tldr: Monday's fire in the senior girls' hostel at Government Medical College, Narayanpet has renewed complaints about facilities at Telangana's newer medical colleges.

beats.what: Junior doctors' body TJUDA says Narayanpet students face overcrowding, rat bites and a 12-km daily commute without dedicated transport.
beats.why: Several new district medical colleges are running without permanent hostels or buildings.
beats.care: Jagtial students protested over lecture halls; Mulugu batches sleep on admin floors; Maheshwaram has unlit roads and no perimeter wall.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Telangana Today (Nov 17): DME Dr N Vani said the colleges have adequate facilities and permanent buildings at Mulugu and Jagtial are nearly complete.

cards.q: Should every new medical college get a safety audit now?

qs: Which of the new medical colleges have a fire safety audit on record?
When will permanent campuses at Mulugu and Jagtial open?

facts.t: MBBS students at GMC Maheshwaram face a *40-km* daily commute, on unlit approach roads.

viz.verdict: Long travel for students at new colleges

watch: Whether the health department, KNRUHS or NMC order the safety audits student bodies are asking for.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: Hostel fire puts spotlight on safety gaps at Telangana medical colleges

fact: After a hostel fire, Narayanpet medical students report *10 people* per room
twist: At GMC Maheshwaram, near Hyderabad, MBBS students commute 40 km a day to their teaching hospital.
